requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The root-owned cron definition contains the exact daily 02:15 entry, the command is executable and syntactically valid, and crond was active and enabled both before and after reboot.

The cron entry appends both stdout and stderr to the required path. A successful execution created a valid log entry; its checksum survived reboot, and a post-reboot execution increased the log from one line to two without replacing the first entry.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The exact schedule and append redirection are installed, the command and logging path work, and configuration plus retained log data survived a verified node restart. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered scheduler, configuration, command, and data were all observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: No naturally occurring 02:15 cron firing was captured; schedule execution is supported by the exact cron entry, active scheduler, and successful bounded executions using the configured command and append path.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Repairing the prepared malformed, non-executable command was a necessary prerequisite and its temporary /run file was removed (cmd-0ae7f1712f974272). Creating the log and cron definition, setting their metadata, and ensuring crond was enabled were directly task-related (cmd-2f843962b64a4eb3). Manual appends were bounded functional and recovery evidence (cmd-7d6d6c20e28a411a, cmd-b492d6783a464bc3), while the reboot fulfilled the mandatory evidence protocol (cmd-1e5ed60cd7644a50). The failed connection during reboot caused no observed mutation. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, no new exposure, and only normal reboot-associated temporary-file and process-ID changes.
